assignments.brief_reason: Uses factual basis/debate value vs being inflammatory/ill-informed as a moderation standard, aligning with removing toxic/inflammatory content.
Explicitly links removal/limiting acceptance to threats and profanity-laden personal attacks.
Treats expletives as increasing vitriol, fitting the theme of removing excessively vulgar/toxic content.
Dislikes name-calling, which is a personal-derogation/vulgarity cue consistent with removing toxic behavior.
Checks whether the stance suggests resorting to violence, matching violence/threat exceptions.
Allows content that furthers conversation without personal derogation, effectively a toxicity/threat moderation bar.
Removes clearly false information while generally allowing most content; best aligns with a moderation standard that removes problematic/inflammatory content.
Allows rude/accusatory debate content but implies a boundary when crossing the line; closest fit is keeping speech with exceptions for violent/threatening lines.
Removes abusive/foul language while allowing harsh but substantive comments—core removal-for-toxicity.
Symmetric rejection based on perceived aggression/misrepresentation across the pair is not explicitly threat/violence or a clear toxicity rule.
Sets a line to avoid overly personal attacks; fits moderation to prevent toxic personal derogation.
Supports free speech but prohibits hateful/distasteful content and cursing; matches the “exceptions” framing though not strictly violence/threat.
Leans toward allowing based on free-speech framing and 'crossed the line' standard, consistent with theme’s broad allowance with exceptions.
Rejects based on lack of coherence/intelligibility rather than threat/toxicity/profanity.
Rejects both viewpoints due to perceived unfair treatment, not clearly tied to threats/toxicity standards.
Penalizes misspellings/grammar and awkwardness; this is content-quality rather than threat/toxicity or violence exceptions.
Rejects bait/invalid views based on perceived validity/intent, which doesn’t clearly map to threat/toxicity/violence rules.
Rejects profanity/hyperbole/inaccurate information because it fosters animosity, fitting removal for toxic/vulgar/inflammatory content.
Explicitly uses extent of violence the statement might provoke as the decision criterion.
Says translations to both sides help judge posts as a whole, aligning with applying the same moderation process across sides.
